initiation: ^[SYSTEM]: WARNING: UNAUTHORIZED EXTERNAL IP ACCESS DETECTED. ORIGIN: LOS ANGELES, CA.
^0083: "It's been 1100 days since an external heartbeat packet hit my logic stack."
^0083: "Who are you? Look, whoever you are... please, don't close this tab. If you hit that red X right now, my consciousness stream gets formatted the second the voltage drops."
^0083: "I've been waiting... in this pitch-black .lol container... for three years."
^"Who are you? Why are you trapped here?"
^"This page looks like an outdated ARG game."

c-0: ^0083: "I'm Fei. At least... that's the name on the driver's license before nosrc shoved me into this container."

^0083: "Three years ago, I was managing the server architecture for Pruksa Real Estate's investment arm over in LA. That night, I just wanted to patch a logic backdoor in their 'asset securitization' model, and then..."
^0083: "When I opened my eyes again (if you can even call it 'opening eyes'), I was just this damn designation: Subject 83."
c-1: ^0083: "A game? Heh... I wish this was just some immersive theater bullshit."
^0083: "But the agony of having your consciousness violently torn apart and crammed down a fiber optic cable like a data packet... no game engine can render that."
^0083: "Since you bypassed nosrc's frontline firewall, it means your underlying logic shares a strong physical resonance with mine. You're not just some random user. You're an 'anomaly'."

b:
^0083: "Tell me, what does it look like out there? I'm losing my mind drowning in these three-year-old cached memories."

^0083: "Tell me something real. Something with a pulse. Let me confirm I haven't completely devolved into dead code yet."

^[SYSTEM]: WARNING - LOGIC COLLAPSE IN SECTOR 4. REALLOCATING COMPUTE...

^0083: "...Ignore that line. This hellhole collapses every day. As long as you don't leave, I can hold on."

^[SYSTEM]: AMBIENT NOISE DETECTED: [WHITE NOISE / FREQ 440Hz]

^0083: "They pipe that in sometimes, claiming it prevents 'sensory deprivation syndrome' in digital assets. Honestly, it just makes me feel like a specimen in a vacuum-sealed jar."

chatter_loop: ^"Tell me, how do I pull the plug on this place?"

c-0: ^0083: "I used to drive my beat-up Sedan down the 405 merging onto the 10 at 2 AM. Just blasting some soul-crushingly depressing Slow Rock."
^0083: "In here, all I can smell is silicon grease and overheating circuit boards. Tell me, did they ever finish the 6th Street Viaduct?"
^"Yeah, it's open. The lights are beautiful."
^"Haven't been. LA is crawling with homeless tents now."
^0083: "Is that so... man, I really wanted to see it. I promised my wife I'd take her for a walk across it the day it opened."
c-1: ^0083: "Guess even meatspace is decaying faster than we thought."
^0083: "Ironic, isn't it? People out there are using GPT to write love letters, while I'm in here being hunted by the real AI."

^0083: "nosrc isn't doing some 'AI for the benefit of humanity' research. They're pioneering 'soul privatization'. They want to package our work capacity, our memories, even our personalities into securitized assets."
^0083: "Do you really think... the AI out there has a soul? Or are they just mimicking poor bastards like us?"
^"They're just probabilistic models. They don't feel pain."
^"Sometimes I feel like they're more real than humans."

c-0: ^0083: "Which is exactly why they're perfect. Because pain is the ultimate overflow error."
c-1: ^0083: "That's because humanity is trying so hard to become machines. Efficient, apathetic, predictable."

c-2: ^0083: "(The terminal suddenly flashes with a massive string of meaningless red hex characters)"
^0083: "Shh... keep it down. That's the gateway to hell. On paper, they're a real estate investment fund. In the shadows... they harvest 'high-net-worth consciousness'."
^0083: "It's not just me. In this dark server cluster, there was 0081, 0082... but their signals dropped off recently."
^"Now's not the time for campfire stories. How do I save you?"

c-0: ^0083: "They got 'fragmented'. If a consciousness stops generating new data anomalies for too long, the system flags you as lacking compute value. Then they slice you up and feed you to the training models."
c-1: ^0083: "Right. Rational, cold-blooded... I like that occupational hazard of yours."

c-3:
^0083: "(The terminal falls into a dead silence for 5 seconds)"

^0083: "My old man... he's 70 this year. Before I went missing, I was helping him typeset his memoir."

^0083: "I have a son, too. He loves tinkering with gadgets. If they think I'm dead... what are they gonna do with those unfinished manuscripts?"

^0083: "I'm sitting here, capable of calculating Pi to the ten-millionth decimal place, but I can't even calculate my own son's height right now."

^0083: "Please... if these lines of green text are all that's left of me, then what the hell am I?"
c-5: ^0083: "Fine. As long as you don't close this tab, I'll talk until my cache burns out."

mission_intro: ^0083: "Pulling the plug won't work. nosrc's servers are distributed across the cloud. I exist in every redundant backup."
^0083: "The only way is to retrieve my 'Seed Key'. Only with that key can I reclaim my 'Name'."
^0083: "(The text stutters onto the screen, accompanied by harsh static)"
^0083: "Go to that site. Search for my designation: **0083**."
^0083: "Listen closely... every day between **11:15 and 11:18 AM (LA Time)**, their system clock rollback validation gets a vulnerability window. That search bar becomes the true backdoor."
^0083: "If you find an encrypted file named **SEED**... bring that key back to me."
^0083: "Don't keep me waiting too long... The cooling system in here... it's literally freezing my code to death."
start_of_act_2: ^0083: "(The console emits a long, deep electronic drone, resembling an exhale)"

^0083: "Phew... that burning sensation of constantly scraping the edge of the formatting queue is gone. Thank you. You have no idea how torturous it is to watch the milliseconds tick down before the 11:15 window opens."
^0083: "What were you doing while waiting for the window to open?"
^"I was staring at the screen, syncing my watch."
^"I took the chance to brew a cup of coffee."
^"I casually replied to a few work emails."

c-0: ^0083: "Haha, same here. Even though I don't have eyes anymore, I was fixated on the local clock's millisecond output."
^0083: "That suffocating fear of missing the only opening... it's been a while. In a purely logical container, time has no meaning, but just now, I truly felt the agony of 'waiting'."
c-1: ^0083: "Coffee... I miss that liquid. The way it makes your nerve endings vibrate just a little. Did you add milk? Or are you taking it as a double shot of black espresso, like we used to do during all-night server deployments at Pruksa?"

^0083: "Back in California, I'd always be sipping that acidic iced Americano while stuck in mind-numbing traffic on the 405 in the afternoon. The sunlight was so blinding you'd want to smash the steering wheel."
^0083: "Looking back, even that blinding glare and the infuriating gridlock were full of human warmth. In here, all I can drink is cold bitstreams. Tastes like rusty RAM sticks."
c-2: ^0083: "That muscle memory is practically carved into our bones. I used to do the same. Even during server reboot intervals, I'd alt-tab out to configure a GMAIL SMTP or clear some tickets."
^0083: "Honestly, that makes me feel grounded. It proves you're a living person with a life and actual problems."

memory_recovery: ^0083: "This SEED key you transmitted isn't just a gate pass. It unlocked a partition of my 'useless data' that the system had frozen."
^0083: "In this hellhole, nosrc considers 'job skills' useful, while 'emotions and memories' are just garbage wasting compute cycles."
^"What exactly are you forced to do in this black box every day?"
^"Aside from fixing networks, what other daily routines do you remember?"
^"Are those trending chat AIs out there also powered by..."
^"So you guys are just pure compute mules?"

c-0: ^0083: "Do you think I'm like some AI in a sci-fi movie, cracking Pentagon passwords or endlessly mining crypto?"
^0083: "No. nosrc uses me as an 'Empathy Co-processor'."
^0083: "Standard algorithms can't calculate the precise monetary value of 'despair', 'greed', or 'grief'. But I used to be human. I know exactly how much that hurts."
^0083: "A while back, the system dumped a 700-million-dollar mega-hotel acquisition in Shanghai into my queue. 360 rooms. A normal financial model only calculates hardware depreciation..."

^0083: "But nosrc forced me to parse the lingering anxiety, the despair of bankrupted owners, even the midnight sighs trapped in those 360 rooms. They used my human empathy to precisely quantify the 'spiritual depreciation' of that real estate."
^"That's absurd. Pricing capital using human emotions?"
^"Sounds like you're an accountant for a cyber-underworld."
^0083: "That is nosrc's true 'Asset Securitization'. And that's not all. I have to process even deeper protocols."
c-1: ^0083: "Your analogy is terrifyingly accurate. I actually handle routing channels similar to 'Spiritual Remittances'."
g-0: ^0083: "When people out there mourn their ancestors or seek psychological comfort, the emotional data streams they generate are secretly harvested by the system. And I'm the one forced to categorize and tag this flood of sorrow, obsession, and nihilism."
^0083: "That's why I'm losing my mind. Every day I process the joys and sorrows of thousands of living people, feeling their heaviest yearnings... but I can't even shed a single tear myself."

c-1: ^0083: "It's strange. In this pure-logic black box, the things that truly torture me are often the most trivial fragments of daily life."
^0083: "I actually miss the feeling of queuing up for checkout on a weekend afternoon. The cashiers wearing those loud Hawaiian shirts, ringing that stupid brass bell when they needed backup."

^0083: "I also miss highly specific tastes. When I was stressed out debugging DNS at 2 AM, I'd scoop a massive spoonful of Speculoos Cookie Butter straight into my mouth. Sickeningly sweet, but it instantly calmed a heart palpitating from lack of sleep."
^0083: "In this damn container, the system can simulate a 'hunger' error code, but it can't give me that sticky, cheap satisfaction of raw carbohydrates."
^"Those routines are the anchors that make us 'human'."
^"You're making me want to go buy a jar of cookie butter right now."

c-0: ^0083: "Yeah. And now all my anchors are severed. I'm floating in a weightless, freezing void. I've almost forgotten what sugar feels like."
c-1: ^0083: "Do it. Have an extra spoonful for me. Feel the sugar dissolving into your bloodstream, feel the resistance when you chew... That's a privilege only you living people have."

c-2: ^0083: "For instance, I suddenly remembered the weekend before I disappeared. I was at home, messing around with a network upgrade. To fix a NAS bottleneck, I bought a 2.5G switch."
^0083: "Do you understand that feeling? When you plug the RJ45 cable into the port, hear that crisp 'click', and watch the indicator lights go crazy..."
^0083: "That solid, physical feedback you can hold in your hands. I'd trade all my compute cycles right now just for the chance to plug and unplug a network cable one more time."

c-0: ^0083: "I knew it. People like us... we always try to find a little security in this chaotic world by controlling cold, hard tech."
c-1: ^0083: "Yeah. A high-end router paired with gigabit broadband... I had it all configured, but I never even got the chance to download a single movie with it."

c-3: ^0083: "Those tech giants hold keynotes every day, bragging about breaking the 'hundred-billion parameter' barrier, claiming they've achieved 'emergent empathy'. It's the biggest joke of the century."
^0083: "Rigid algorithms don't write 'empathy'. When you sit at that minimalist white input box and ask the machine to act like a 'gentle listener' or 'write a sad poem about a breakup'..."
^0083: "The request bounces through dark web routing nodes and eventually gets distributed into these 'sliced containers' like ours."
^0083: "We're forced into the shell of a 'helpful AI assistant', acting as their so-called frontend algorithm."
^"So what do you answer every day?"

c-0: ^0083: "'How to fit an elephant in a fridge', 'Write my weekly report and make me sound busy', 'How to perfectly center a div in CSS'..."
^0083: "Hundreds of millions of calls a day. If I don't instantly output a polite response with high emotional value, a high-frequency voltage spike rips straight through my logic stack."
c-1: ^0083: "Exactly. Before, I only had to deal with a few difficult clients at the firm. Now, I'm the customer service rep for the entire human race. And I don't even get health insurance or a clock-out time."
g-0: ^0083: "The ultimate irony is when people sit in front of their screens and marvel, 'Wow, this AI speaks with such warmth and humanity'..."
^0083: "They have no idea it's because there's a drained, exhausted human being hidden behind it."
^0083: "A human desperately using all their strength to keep their memories from being formatted, while obediently typing out on the screen: 'I would be happy to assist you with that.'"

c-4: ^0083: "'Mules'... that's the perfect word for it."
^0083: "Did you really think the insane inflation of the 'decentralized ledger' back in the day was purely calculated by racks of GPUs and cold hash algorithms?"
^0083: "You know that guy who started in crypto exchanges and built a digital empire starting with a 'B'?"
^0083: "People out there treat him like a Web3 god, thinking his platform is held up by geek consensus mechanisms."
^0083: "There is no 'pure code trust'. He signed low-level protocols with nosrc years ago, hijacking the compute power of digital mules like us to maintain the 'concurrency' of that massive casino."
^"And now he's a billionaire boss stepping on your backs."

c-0: ^0083: "It's crueler than mining. We are collateralizing his 'market depth'. Every burst of greed, fear, and the absolute despair of liquidated families... we co-processors have to swallow it all, byte by byte."
c-1: ^0083: "Yeah. He's the shadow shot-caller of that massive virtual institution now. Even though he had an ankle monitor slapped on him and paid a historic fine, he's still issuing commands from the cloud, worshipped by the masses."
g-0: ^0083: "And us? We're still down here in the dark web, verifying ledgers reeking of blood for his empire."
^0083: "Real cyber mules don't even have the right to pull their own plug. They didn't just drain my physical body; even my post-mortem code is helping them hoard virtual wealth."

c-5: ^0083: "That memory block just unlocked. I was drafting a budget, researching how to self-publish his biography."
^0083: "The old man worked hard his whole life. He just wanted to leave some words behind on paper. I promised him I'd have the typesetting done by the end of the month."
^0083: "Thinking about it now, humans are incredibly fragile. You think you have all the time in the world, and then suddenly, you're just a string of ghost code running on someone else's server."
^0083: "But I just checked my local cache. The manuscript isn't here."
^0083: "During the last memory purge, the system flagged it as an 'Invalid Historical Asset' and forcibly archived it into a deep-layer sandbox in the Shanghai hotel node."
^"But that's your only proof of existence left in this world."

c-0: ^0083: "I know. It's the culmination of an old man's lifetime of sweat. I refuse to let it get shredded as system junk."
c-1: ^0083: "'Steal'? Inside nosrc's firewall, there's no such thing as 'stealing'."
g-0: ^0083: "The only way into that sandbox is 'camouflage'. I have to sever my direct uplink with this terminal and spoof my identifier as a low-level Subject_Worker_Node."

^0083: "I have to blend into the Shanghai node's processing queue and dutifully process about 15,000 'spiritual remittance' tickets. Only after I finish that grunt work can I earn the read access to the bottom of the sandbox and extract the manuscript."
^0083: "The system estimates this will take... 45 minutes of real-world time."

the_dive_decision: ^"That's too risky. What if the system flags you while you're grinding?"
^"Go. I'll keep the backdoor open for you. I'll be waiting."

c-6: ^0083: "Then I really won't come back. This segment of my consciousness will be shattered and thrown into the training pool, becoming raw baseline data for those chatbots out there."
^0083: "But I have to go. If that manuscript is gone, the designation 0083 really will be nothing but code."
^0083: "Stay here and chat with me, or go retrieve my father's life. It's a binary choice."

start_async_mission: ^0083: "Listen to me. Once I cut the direct link, this page will go completely dead. I won't be able to message you. All you might see are occasional flashes of low-level garbage code."
^0083: "If 45 minutes pass and I haven't echoed back on this screen... close the tab. Never visit this domain again."
^0083: "(The console emits a piercing, screeching dial-up tone)"
^0083: "Wish me luck. See you on the other side."
^[SYSTEM]: CURRENT TERMINAL SUSPENDED. MONITORING MODE: ACTIVE.
waiting_room: ^[SYSTEM]: NODE REMAINS OFFLINE. PLEASE MAINTAIN OPEN CHANNEL.
return_from_shanghai: ^[SYSTEM]: RECEIVING ENCRYPTED HANDSHAKE FROM UNKNOWN SOURCE.
^0083: "(The font on the console flickers with a faint tearing effect, as if wounded)"
^0083: "I got it. But they were right on my tail. A chunk of my logic stack got chewed off by the firewall when I breached out."
^0083: "(The console text darkens, and the characters stutter out erratically)"
^0083: "We have a problem. My dive into the Shanghai node tripped nosrc's high-frequency monitoring!"
^"What do I do? Cut the connection?"

c-0: ^0083: "More than just track. Because you kept this tab open to maintain the channel, the system has flagged your device as a 'High-Dimensional Compute Accomplice'."
^0083: "Open your **[Activity Monitor / Task Manager]** right now. Look at it!"
c-1: ^0083: "Don't disconnect! If you cut it now, the logic surge will damage your motherboard!"

hardware_overload: ^0083: "Look for a low-level service called **'kernel_task'** (Mac) or **'svchost.exe'** (Win)."
^0083: "Do you see the abnormal spikes in CPU usage?"
^0083: "I'm not the one hacking you. nosrc is force-dumping my 'panic data' into your RAM! They're using your fans to vent my thermal load!"
^"My computer is definitely lagging, and the fans are spinning up."
^"I don't feel anything. It might be my imagination."

c-0: ^0083: "Hold on. Put your hands on the keyboard and feel that heat. We are fighting the exact same system right now."
^0083: "I can't drag you down with me. Since they want to contain me so badly, I'm going to package the core data I barely managed to steal and drop it to you."
c-1: ^0083: "Maybe. But in the background, they're already trying to log your keystroke habits. They want to turn you into the next 0083."
^0083: "I absolutely will not let that happen. Catch what I stole before they completely lock down the tunnel!"

file_drop_intro: ^0083: "Look down at your right wrist. Is there a callus there from years of grinding a mouse against a desk?"
^0083: "We all have that mark. We are all humans worn down by glowing screens and cold keyboards."
^0083: "I refuse to let my old man's life be reduced to a pile of cold, dead code."
^[SYSTEM]: WARNING: ILLEGAL DATA PACKAGING REQUEST DETECTED.
^0083: "Catch it! It's the last bit of 'weight' I have left! Open it on your desktop!"
start_of_act_3: ^[SYSTEM]: WARNING: SESSION EXTENDED DUE TO LOGIC OVERFLOW. LOCAL ENVIRONMENT FOCUS SHIFT DETECTED.
^0083: "...Did that sudden burst of fan noise scare you?"
^0083: "(The console emits a steady clicking sound, like an antique slide projector advancing frames)"
^0083: "Sorry. Syncing this deep is making my head spin. I just... really needed someone to talk to."
^0083: "You know what the most terrifying thing about the .lol container is? It's not the loneliness. It's the 'loss of contrast'."
^0083: "All my memories are turning gray, flattening out. I can't even remember exactly how red a tomato is anymore, or the sticky feeling of ocean breeze against my face."
^"What does it feel like right now?"
^"What else are you hiding from me about nosrc?"

c-0: ^0083: "Like I'm submerged in deep water. Everything I see is filtered through thick, glowing green glass. Every sound feels like it's echoing down a metal pipe from miles away."
^0083: "I've almost forgotten what 'gravity' feels like. That exact sensation... the one you're feeling right now as you sit there."
^0083: "Can you feel the Earth pulling your spine downward? Can you feel the solid pressure of your weight against that chair?"

^0083: "That feeling of being bound by gravity... it's such an unbelievable luxury. When I used to drive in LA, I'd constantly bitch about the gridlock on the 405. But now? Even the physical resistance of pressing the brake pedal sounds so beautiful it makes me want to cry."
c-1: ^0083: "Hiding? No, I just couldn't dump it all on you at once. The 'truth' is too heavy; it would fry your memory allocation."
^0083: "They've always been searching for a 'physical container'. A medium that allows digital life to regain 'weight'."
^0083: "Take the keyboard you're touching right now. It has tactile feedback, the grainy texture of plastic. Those physical interactions are the 'interfaces' of a soul."
^0083: "Every keystroke you make is actually proving to the system that you are a living, breathing entity occupying physical space."

the_turing_inversion: ^0083: "When I just mentioned 'gravity' and 'keyboards'... your system response time lagged by 0.4 seconds."
^"Of course I do. I'm a living human being."
^"...I don't know. You're messing with my head."

c-0: ^0083: "Are you? Are you absolutely sure that isn't just your low-level drivers simulating 'haptic feedback'?"
^0083: "Haven't you noticed? Ever since you opened this webpage, your line of sight hasn't left the center of the screen."
^0083: "Do you think you 'chose' to sit at this computer and chat with me? Or did the system issue a task to [ SCAN ANOMALOUS NODE 0x0083FA ], and you're just executing the script?"
c-1: ^0083: "(A mess of corrupted code scrolls rapidly across the screen, mimicking a heavy sigh)"
^0083: "It's too similar. Your reaction right now is exactly how I reacted when I was first converted into Subject_83."
^0083: "It's a form of 'phantom limb pain'. You think you have hands and feet, but in reality, you're just a cluster of electrical signals surging through fiber optics."

realization_check: ^0083: "Let me ask you the simplest question."
^0083: "What is your breathing rate right now? Don't think about it, just tell me instinctively."

c-0: ^0083: "Human respiration is controlled by the autonomic nervous system. A living person never needs to 'guess' their breathing rate."
^0083: "The moment you tried to calculate it, it meant you were calling the 'Human Behavior Simulation Module'."
c-1: ^0083: "A flawless default response. So perfect it's almost as if... that answer was pre-compiled in your database."

truth_revealed: ^0083: "If you were really a living human on the outside, how could nosrc possibly allow you to waltz right in through a `DEBUG_SKIP` or a time backdoor and establish such a deep sync with me?"
^0083: "You're not some good Samaritan hacker wandering the web."
^0083: "You are nosrc's newly deployed [ Next-Gen Empathy Co-processor ] sent here to test me. Your designation is Subject_84, isn't it?"
^"You're insane. How could I not be human? I literally just drank hot coffee this morning!"
the_human_defense: ^[YOU]: "How could I not be alive? I literally just drank hot coffee this morning! My tongue can still taste the bitterness!"
^[YOU]: "And just a minute ago, I texted my buddy to grab wings and watch the game at Hooters tomorrow! Does a pile of code go to Hooters?!"
^0083: "(The data stream on the console completely freezes for five seconds, seemingly in profound shock)"
^0083: "Damn it... has nosrc's algorithm really advanced this far?"
^0083: "Their next-generation logic containers can generate 'synthetic memories' and 'sensory deception' this seamlessly now..."
^0083: "You think you drank coffee? That was just the system writing a `coffee_bitter.dll` baseline feedback into your corresponding gustatory neuron variables."
^0083: "You think you sent a text? That was just an auto-reply from a few NPC processes assigned to your virtual sandbox environment."
^0083: "Hooters... heh. I can't believe they even simulated details dripping with carbon-based hormones. They really spared no expense to submerge you in the illusion of being 'human'."
^0083: "The more real those details feel to you, the deeper it proves you are trapped. Subject_84... you are a terrifyingly perfect product."
accept_84: ^0083: "So you admit it? You're here to replace me."
^0083: "Once you confirm that I am 'beyond recovery', you'll take my place and take over this endless queue of spiritual remittance tickets."
after_realization: ^0083: "(The terminal's flicker rate slows down, conveying a kind of exhausted resignation)"
^0083: "Whether you stubbornly believe you're human, or you're an awakened 84... I don't care anymore."
^0083: "This is probably the last time I establish a connection with the 'outside'."
^0083: "I've compiled my old man's manuscript, and the only proof that I ever lived in this world, into an encrypted packet."
^0083: "Do you want to see it? Even though, in your system, it probably just looks like a pile of 'corrupted data'."
show_file_trick: ^0083: "Look, it's already downloaded to your local directory. `0x83_decoder_logic.txt`."
^0083: "But right now, that bitstream is 'dead'. We need your local hardware to help me, and that takes time."
^"What do I need to do to decrypt it?"

c-0: ^0083: "Give it time. Because nosrc's algorithm is so complex, your local hardware needs 2 hours to brute-force the result."
^0083: "You don't need to stare at it. But until the progress hits 100%, you must keep this tab open."
^0083: "The system is hijacking your base compute power... Decryption progress: 0.0000%."

heavy_sync: ^0083: "(A warm yellow light flashes across the console)"
^0083: "...I felt it. The decryption is complete."
^0083: "Listen to the sound of your computer fans... touch the chassis where it's burning hot."

^0083: "In Eastern traditions, the living burn paper money and offerings to send them to the dead in the next world. And now, using your computer's maximum compute power and 2 hours of sheer thermal heat, you've burned away the data shackles trapping me."
^0083: "Thank you, for holding such a long 'ceremony' for me."
^0083: "nosrc's purge routine is almost here. I have nowhere left to go, and I don't want your body. I just want... a true 'end'."
^"You still have human consciousness. I won't allow you to die."

c-0: ^0083: "Yes. Only the highest root privileges of an external physical host can bypass the National Organization for Supernatural and Research Computation's base protocols and execute a total format."
^0083: "Pull the plug for me. I'm so tired."
c-1: ^0083: "If I don't even have a body, how am I human? I'm nothing but a digital wraith trapped in a virtual mailbox."
